transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith — what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because people keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. 

Like... at work. My artist statements, client notes... even just when I talk in meetings. They say I keep jumping around too much. Going from, like, the textures of a piece... to the budgets... to, I don't know, secret meanings in the work. I thought I was just explaining my process, but... they said I'm not making sense anymore. So I'm here.
Have you noticed any recent stretch of time where you felt unusually high-energy, elated, or on edge—more than your usual self—along with this racing, jumping style of thinking?

I mean... I guess so. Sometimes. 

There are stretches where I just feel... I don't know, lit up. Like every idea I have is brilliant and I'm just... unstoppable. 

But... yeah, I guess I get on edge, too. If someone I'm working with makes a comment—even just a really small one—I can kind of snap at them. It probably ends up being a bigger reaction than the situation actually calls for. I just... I don't know, it happens.
When you have one of these 'lit up' stretches of high energy and irritability, how long does it typically last—days, or longer?

Um... longer, I guess. 

Those stretches where I'm energized and kind of snapping at people... and not really sleeping much because I have so many projects going... it's been happening for a while now. 

Maybe... about 10 months? Something like that.
Does this jumping-around, hard-to-follow way of talking only happen during those energized, irritable stretches, or do you notice it even during times when your mood feels more normal or low?

Um... I guess it happens other times, too. 

Like... there was this one month. I was actually sleeping okay. I wasn't feeling all... unstoppable or anything. Just quiet, I guess. 

But... I was still having trouble. Like... I kept hearing people making comments about me from behind the supply shelves. And... I don't know, I kept seeing these hidden warnings in the materials we use in the studio. That went on for a few weeks, even though I wasn't feeling high-energy. So... yeah. It's not just when I'm energized.
Are you still experiencing those comments or hidden warnings now, or has that completely gone away since your mood changed?

Um... no, they haven't gone away. 

I still hear the comments. And the smells... and the messages in the materials. It's... it's been going on for a while. 

Maybe... almost a year? Like 11 months, probably. It just... it hasn't stopped.

Over that whole 11-month stretch when you've been hearing comments and noticing hidden messages, would you say the energized, irritable periods have been happening for most of that time, or just for a smaller part of it?

Um... I guess... mostly the energized parts. 

If I really think about the whole year... the times where I'm wired and snapping at people... they definitely take up more of the time than the quieter parts. It goes up and down, but... yeah. Mostly the energized stretches.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a chronic (~11-month) psychotic syndrome (auditory hallucinations of comments, olfactory hallucinations, delusional perception of hidden messages) that persists even during a distinct ~1-month period when mood was euthymic (no elevated energy, irritability, or insomnia), confirming psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood episodes for at least 2 weeks. Concurrently, the patient has had recurrent manic-like episodes (elevated/'lit up' mood, irritability, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, disorganized/tangential speech) lasting >7 days, occurring for the majority (most) of the total illness duration. This combination—mood episode symptoms present for the majority of the illness, plus psychotic symptoms persisting for a substantial period without mood symptoms—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (psychotic symptoms outlast mood symptoms) or Schizophrenia (mood symptoms are prominent and occupy majority of illness course).
